subject: general
question: A dealer allows a 30% discount on the marked price of an item. What is the marked price of the item if its sale price is ₹12,460?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **ratio method**: 30% discount → 3/10 (where 10 is **Marked Price** and 3 is **Discount**).

**Selling Price (SP)** = 10 − 3 = 7 units.

Given 7 units = ₹12,460.

1 unit = 12,460 ÷ 7 = ₹1,780.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 10 units = 1,780 × 10 = ₹17,800.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹17,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Discount Percentage** = 30%

**Sale Price (SP)** = ₹12,460

**Formula Used:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = [**Sale Price** ÷ (100 − **Discount%**)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9a2e89ce3f3533268c9e8f979cc16b695bf90bce23a77a3acf72c6dbae8849e8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Marked Price** be **x**.

⇒ **SP** = **x** × (100 − 30)/100

⇒ 12,460 = **x** × 70/100

⇒ 12,460 = 0.70 × **x**

⇒ **x** = 12,460 ÷ 0.70

⇒ **x** = 124,600 ÷ 7

⇒ **x** = 17,800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹17,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price printed on the label of an article, also known as the **List Price**. Discounts are always calculated on this value.

Successive Discount

When two or more discounts are applied one after another, the single equivalent discount is given by: [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100]%.

Profit/Loss on Marked Price

To find **Cost Price (CP)** when **Profit %** and **Discount %** are given: **CP/MP** = (100 − **Discount%**) / (100 + **Profit%**).
